findings: No minimum RRT segment count or 80-second episode requirement found in the reviewed downstream path/timing/source/quality/RGB gates. Two-node nonzero simplified paths are admissible in principle.

A one-node path is rejected at original TOPP admission. Exact duplicates may collapse to one no-motion row, then original motion/source binding requires >=2 rows and rejects incomplete planning evidence.

A nonzero segment whose installed native TOPP duration supplies fewer than two samples is rejected unchanged; component tiny segment reproduces this. No interpolation/resampling or relaxed minimum added.
Precontact numerical quality requires >=2 actual 60ms observations as well as physical samples. Contact before adequate evidence remains a rejection; no relaxation introduced.

Native simplification may produce a new edge that fails complete mesh or timing/dense velocity gates, or changes physical tracking/contact. These remain mandatory real collection rejection conditions.
scope: Read-only reviewed original source plus actual original TOPP CPU tiny-model cases; no SAPIEN scene or GPU, no real randomized robot trajectory acceptance
